deep.reconstruction:
Context: a fundamental system (y_1,...,y_n) of a class of multivalued functions with branch points a,b,...,g. A positive loop around a acts by the linear substitution (A). On the previous page (A) was diagonalized as (A) = (α) diag(λ_1,...,λ_n) (α)^{-1}, assuming distinct eigenvalues. The new functions z = (α)^{-1} y therefore satisfy z_k -> λ_k z_k under the loop.

This page: local exponents at a.

(1) Lemma. Suppose z picks up the factor λ under a positive loop around a. The function (x-a)^μ = exp(μ log(x-a)) picks up exp(2πi μ), because log(x-a) increases by 2πi. Choose μ = log(λ)/(2πi), so that e^{2πiμ} = λ. Then z(x-a)^{-μ} is single-valued ("einändrig") in a punctured neighbourhood of a. Its Laurent expansion is z(x-a)^{-μ} = Σ_{m∈Z} c_m (x-a)^m. Hence z = Σ c_m (x-a)^{μ+m}, a series in powers whose exponents differ from μ by integers. [Implicit, mine: μ is fixed only mod Z by the branch of log, which is harmless.]

(2) Applied to z_k. Each z_k expands in powers (x-a)^{log(λ_k)/(2πi)+m}, m∈Z.

(3) Hypothesis. The y's nowhere become infinite of infinite order, i.e. there are no essential singularities (the regular-singular or Fuchsian condition). Then each Laurent series terminates on the side of negative powers. Let μ_k be the lowest exponent occurring. Then z_k(x-a)^{-μ_k} is finite and nonzero at x=a.

(4) Consequences.
- Since e^{2πiμ_k} = λ_k and the λ_k are pairwise distinct, no difference μ_j - μ_k (j≠k) is an integer.
- Conversely, for two systems of the same class (same monodromy, hence the same λ's, which are fixed by (A)), the corresponding exponents differ only by integers.

The next page continues: these exponents, together with (α), characterize a system. This leads to the P-symbol notation Q(a..g; (α)..(ϑ); μ_k, ν_k, ..., ϱ_k; x).
errors: No mathematical errors. Two points are implicit: the choice of branch of log λ (μ is defined only mod 1), and a nonzero leading coefficient after possibly shifting μ by an integer. Both are handled correctly by defining μ_k as the lowest exponent actually occurring.

The claim that exponents of same-class systems differ by integers relies on λ_k being determined by (A). Strictly, the eigenvalues are determined only up to the ordering of the diagonal, so 'corresponding' presupposes a matching ordering. This is a minor tacit convention.

results.what: A function multiplied by λ under a loop around a equals (x-a)^μ times a single-valued function, with μ = log λ/(2πi). Its expansion has exponents in μ+Z.
results.modern_name: Local monodromy / exponent of a multiplicative-monodromy function (local Floquet-type decomposition)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1857 P-function paper; Nachlass 'Zwei allgemeine Lehrsätze' published in Werke 1876). Fuchs (1866) did this independently in the ODE setting.

results.what: Under the no-essential-singularity hypothesis, the local exponents μ_k are lowest exponents. With distinct monodromy eigenvalues, their differences are non-integers. Exponents within a class are determined mod Z by the monodromy.
results.modern_name: Regular singular point; local exponents with exp(2πi μ_k) = eigenvalues of local monodromy (non-resonant case)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 / Nachlass (Werke 1876); Fuchs 1866 (Fuchsian condition, indicial equation)

deep.surprise_reason: This page belongs to Riemann's posthumous memoir on linear ODEs with algebraic coefficients. That memoir was printed in his Gesammelte Werke (1876), and its content (exponents from monodromy, the P-symbol) is well known as his.

checkable.asserts: The choice μ = log λ/(2πi) gives e^{2πiμ} = λ.
(x-a)^μ acquires the factor e^{2πiμ} under a positive loop, since log(x-a) increases by 2πi.
Exponents differing by integers give the same multiplier λ. Hence distinct λ's force non-integer exponent differences.
